title: Integer-shift coherence for a prescribed pair-category functor
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and noetherian finite-dimensional schemes $T,S$ on which $\ell$ is invertible. For $H=T,S$, use the finite-stage categories $\mathcal C_E(H)$ and pair category $\mathcal P_H$ of [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category], with their canonical integer shifts and inclusion functors $j_E^H$ from [prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus]. Write $\sigma^H_{F/E,n,K}:T^H_{F/E}(K[n])\xrightarrow{\sim}(T^H_{F/E}K)[n]$ for the iterated scalar shift comparisons of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. Use the meaning of exact functor from [def-weil-triangulated-category].

Let $\Phi_E:\mathcal C_E(T)\to\mathcal C_E(S)$ be additive functors [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor] equipped with natural isomorphisms $s_{E,n,K}:\Phi_E(K[n])\xrightarrow{\sim}(\Phi_EK)[n]$ for every $n\in\mathbf Z$, satisfying the zero and addition coherence equations. Let $\beta_{F/E}:T^S_{F/E}\Phi_E\xrightarrow{\sim}\Phi_F T^T_{F/E}$ be natural isomorphisms satisfying $\beta_{E/E}=1$ and
$$\beta_{G/E,K}\circ a^S_{G,F,E,\Phi_EK}=\Phi_G(a^T_{G,F,E,K})\circ\beta_{G/F,T^T_{F/E}K}\circ T^S_{G/F}(\beta_{F/E,K})$$
for $E\subseteq F\subseteq G$. Suppose, for every $E\subseteq F$, $n$ and $K$, that
$$s_{F,n,T^T_{F/E}K}\circ\Phi_F(\sigma^T_{F/E,n,K})\circ\beta_{F/E,K[n]}=(\beta_{F/E,K})[n]\circ\sigma^S_{F/E,n,\Phi_EK}\circ T^S_{F/E}(s_{E,n,K}).$$
Let $G:\mathcal P_T\to\mathcal P_S$ be an additive functor with object formula $G(E,K)=(E,\Phi_EK)$ and representative formula
$$G[M,u]=[M,\beta_{M/F,L}^{-1}\circ\Phi_M(u)\circ\beta_{M/E,K}]$$
for $u:T^T_{M/E}K\to T^T_{M/F}L$.

Then $s_{n,(E,K)}=[E,s_{E,n,K}]$ are the components of natural isomorphisms $s_n:G(-[n])\xrightarrow{\sim}(G-)[n]$. They satisfy the zero and addition coherence equations. Explicitly, for categories $\mathcal A=\mathcal P_T$, $\mathcal B=\mathcal P_S$, write $z^H_X:X[0]\xrightarrow{\sim}X$ and $c^H_{n,m,X}:X[n+m]\xrightarrow{\sim}(X[n])[m]$ for the canonical shift identifications, where $H=\mathcal A,\mathcal B$. Then
$$s_{0,X}=(z^{\mathcal B}_{GX})^{-1}\circ G(z^{\mathcal A}_X),$$
$$s_{n+m,X}=(c^{\mathcal B}_{n,m,GX})^{-1}\circ(s_{n,X})[m]\circ s_{m,X[n]}\circ G(c^{\mathcal A}_{n,m,X}).$$
Moreover there is a natural isomorphism $\kappa_E:Gj_E^T\xrightarrow{\sim}j_E^S\Phi_E$ with identity components. It is compatible with these shift comparisons: if $s^{Gj_E^T}$ and $s^{j_E^S\Phi_E}$ denote the composite shift comparisons, then
$$s^{j_E^S\Phi_E}_{n,K}\circ\kappa_{E,K[n]}=(\kappa_{E,K})[n]\circ s^{Gj_E^T}_{n,K}.$$
No preservation of distinguished triangles by $G$ is assumed or concluded.

proof.text: The prescribed object and representative formulas identify G with the existing A.functor. Apply Functor.hext to the object formula and use PairCategory.hom_induction on an arbitrary morphism; on a representative the required heterogeneous equality is exactly the assumed map formula. This avoids any need to normalize equal-field transitions or beta components.

proof.text: For each integer n, regard the stage shift comparisons s_{i,n} as a Morphism.Hom from shift_n.comp A to A.comp shift_n. Expand the two composite beta components. The compatibility equation is exactly NatTrans.shift_app_comm for beta, with Functor.commShiftIso_comp_hom_app. Descend this Hom by Morphism.descNatTrans. Its naturality, the functorCompIso comparisons and the images under the target stage inclusions of the stage comparison isomorphisms give a natural isomorphism shift_n followed by A.functor to A.functor followed by shift_n. The functorCompIso components are identities, so its hom component is precisely the included s_{i,n}.

proof.text: Verify the zero law componentwise. The common-stage zero comparison is the image of the stage zero comparison. Morphism.functor_map_iota (Lean: functor_map_ι) rewrites the image of this comparison under A.functor. Apply the target inclusion functor to the stage functor CommShift zero axiom; preservation of composition gives exactly the required pair-category zero axiom.

proof.text: Verify the addition law for arbitrary integers n,m componentwise. The common-stage addition comparisons are included stage comparisons. The functor_map_ι equations for A and the stage shift rewrite their images, and the included stage CommShift addition axiom gives the pair-category addition axiom. No sign restriction or iteration argument is needed, and the canonical comparison for opposite integers is retained.

proof.text: Take kappa_i to be the existing A.ιCompFunctorIso i, whose components are identities. Expand NatTrans.CommShift and the two composite functor shift comparisons. The inclusion comparisons are identities; the descended comparison at the included object is the included stage comparison by step 2. Functors preserve identities, so both sides agree. Transfer the structure, component formulas and inclusion comparison along the equality G = A.functor from step 1.

lean.note: PairFunctorShiftCoherenceSpec packages every displayed hypothesis and conclusion over the existing stage systems; the theorem specializes that predicate to the concrete normalized PBC systems, avoiding repeated unfolding of concrete quotient Hom types. G remains arbitrary with its prescribed object and representative formulas; no triangle preservation is assumed or concluded. The helper is the statement predicate, not a new mathematical construction.
